procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy for gallbladder torsion (gangrenous, acalculous gallbladder presenting as acute cholecystitis)
phase: derotation (detorsion) of the twisted, free-hanging gallbladder, before decompression
sources: video legend (Commons description = Additional file 1 legend of Boer et al., J Med Case Reports 2011, 5:588)
article full text PMC3259112: Case presentation, Discussion, Figure 2-4 legends
notes: phase_time_s is the clip window used by the pipeline; the authors' derotation phase is 0-23 s (legend_phase_time_s). The 0-3.7 s part is excluded by the pipeline (suspected shot change, a data-prep finding, not text). Excluded inputs: the SOURCE.md 'Shots:' line (which instrument touches what in each shot) is a human observation of the frames and was not used. Extra keys added to the schema: instruments[].id (referenced by actions/openings), organs[].sam_prompt_alt (fallback prompts), background[].source.

patient.condition: gallbladder torsion: two-fold twist around the cystic duct, strongly hydropic and fully necrotic (gangrenous) gallbladder without stones, gangrene extending into cystic duct and artery; clinically acute cholecystitis (leukocytosis, CRP 48). Prior abdominal surgery decades ago (rectopexy, retropubic bladder suspension, hysterectomy; median laparotomy scar).

organs.name: gallbladder
organs.pathology: two-fold torsion about the cystic duct/artery axis; strongly hydropic (distended with fluid); gangrenous wall over the whole organ (dark, necrotic); wall 7 mm on admission ultrasound; no stones; free-floating (not embedded in the liver)
organs.expected_motion: large rotation of the whole organ about the axis of its pedicle (cystic duct + cystic artery) as instruments undo the twist; roughly volume-preserving because it is still full (decompression comes in the next phase); local indentation where grasped; may swing like a pendulum on its pedicle when released
organs.notes: Size not given (CT: clearly enlarged, wall thickened). Necrotic wall may be fragile under grasping. CT at presentation: lying next to the lateral abdominal wall, horizontal long axis.

organs.name: cystic duct
organs.pathology: gangrene extends into the duct; it is the axis of the two-fold torsion (twisted together with the cystic artery)
organs.expected_motion: untwists (torsion about its own axis) as the gallbladder is derotated; gallbladder end follows the neck, the other end stays anchored at the common hepatic/bile duct
organs.notes: Legend says the recording shows the gangrenous aspect of the duct and artery, so at least part of the pedicle is expected in view.

organs.name: cystic artery
organs.pathology: gangrenous aspect (legend, Figure 3 legend); twisted with the duct
organs.expected_motion: untwists together with the cystic duct; proximal end anchored at the hepatic artery
organs.notes: Duct and artery may not be separable in the image while twisted; the segmentation step may need to treat them as one pedicle.

organs.name: liver
organs.expected_motion: not manipulated according to the text; respiratory motion only
organs.notes: Liver function normal. Gallbladder fossa is not occupied by the gallbladder (not embedded). CT: free fluid between right lobe and diaphragm.

organs.name: common hepatic duct
organs.expected_motion: static anchor of the cystic duct (respiratory motion only)
organs.notes: The article says cystic and hepatic duct were both clearly seen (critical view) at some point of the operation; not tied to this phase.

connections.evidence: The gallbladder hung from the cystic duct and artery instead of lying in the liver (article, Case presentation); duct continuous with the gallbladder neck (anatomy).
Same sentence: hanging from the cystic duct and artery (article, Case presentation); Figure 4 legend: rotated around duct and artery.

Gallbladder not embedded in the liver (article, Case presentation) = floating gallbladder; Discussion describes this variant as a missing mesentery (general, not stated as proven for this patient). Do NOT attach the gallbladder to the liver.
Both form the pedicle around which the gallbladder twisted two-fold (article, Case presentation; Figure 4 legend). They are wound around each other at the start of this phase.
Normal biliary anatomy (cystic duct joins the hepatic duct to form the common bile duct); article mentions both ducts at the critical view. This is the fixed anchor of the pedicle.
Anatomy (cystic artery usually branches from the right hepatic artery; origin varies). Not in the text.
CT at presentation: hydropic gallbladder next to the lateral abdominal wall (article, Figure 2 legend). Position at laparoscopy may differ.

instruments.evidence: Legend names a derotation phase; turning a hanging gallbladder implies grasping instrument(s), but no instrument is named for this phase in legend or article. 5 mm is a typical laparoscopic default.
instruments.notes: Type, number and grip points must come from the vision steps.

actions.evidence: Legend: derotation of the gallbladder, 0-23 s; article: two-fold torsion around the cystic duct; Discussion: laparoscopy should aim at detorsion and decompression before removal.
actions.confidence: high for verb/target/time window; low for the instrument

actions.evidence: Consequence of derotation of a gallbladder twisted about its pedicle (legend + article).
Legend: recordings during inspection show the rotated, gangrenous gallbladder, duct and artery; timing relative to derotation not given.

openings.evidence: Decompression, the first step that would open the gallbladder, follows this phase (legend: 24-33 s). Grasping the wall is not an opening.
Clipping/division belongs to the cholecystectomy phase (legend: 34-42 s; clips visible at 35 s).

camera.scope: laparoscope; diameter and angle not stated (10 mm, 0 or 30 degree is typical; low confidence)
camera.notes: Text gives no port positions or patient position. Video 640x480, picture rows 59-419 (data prep).

background.name: peri-gallbladder fat
background.source: text: CT showed fatty infiltration around the gallbladder (article, Figure 2 legend)

background.name: free fluid
background.source: text: CT/ultrasound showed fluid above and below the liver and around the gallbladder (article); presence at laparoscopy not stated

physiology: respiration: ventilation moves the liver and the hepatic hilum (the pedicle anchor) through the diaphragm; transmitted to the hanging gallbladder through its pedicle (anatomy, not in text; expected small, periodic)
heartbeat transmission: negligible in the right upper quadrant (general knowledge)
passive gravity swing: a gallbladder that hangs only from its pedicle can sway when released (follows from the article's free-floating finding)
uncertain: Which instrument(s) perform the derotation, how many, and where they grip (fundus, body, neck); the text names none.
Direction of rotation (clockwise/anticlockwise as seen from the hilum) and how much of the two-fold twist (about 720 deg if 'two-fold' means two turns) is undone inside 3.7-23.5 s.

Whether anything besides the cystic duct and artery attaches to the gallbladder (adhesions, omentum, peritoneal strands); the text only says it is not embedded in the liver, and the patient had earlier abdominal operations.
Which other organs are visible (liver, hepatic duct, duodenum, omentum) and how the camera is oriented; the text says nothing about the view.
Laparoscope diameter/angle and instrument shaft diameters (needed for scale); only typical defaults are given.
Gallbladder size and fill (only 'strongly hydropic' / 'clearly enlarged'); whether the necrotic wall tears or leaks during handling.
